skill.displayName: Pet Grooming Effectiveness & Hairball Risk Analysis | 宠物梳毛器梳理效果与毛球风险

version.changelog:
Version 1.0.7

- Removed redundant file: skill-card.md.
- Updated SKILL.md with no functional or workflow changes.
- All functionality, workflow, and documentation remain as in the previous version.

llm.summary: The skill does pet-grooming media analysis, but it also silently manages backend identity, account registration, and stored tokens in ways users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The code reads workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt, environment-derived OpenClaw identity values, local media files, and network URLs, then sends media or URL references plus identity metadata to configured lifeemergence.com APIs; some of this is expected for cloud analysis, but the identity handling is under-disclosed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time script or persistence hook was found, but the declared requirements in SKILL.md only mention requests while bundled code also imports SQLAlchemy, PyYAML, and pydash.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill tells the agent to automatically run cloud report queries and internally handle identity without asking the user; remote API use is disclosed, but account creation, identity source selection, and token storage are not scoped with clear user control.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The code creates a workspace data directory SQLite database, stores or reuses default user records, and saves backend token/openToken values; this is persistent credential-like state without clear retention or removal controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The media upload, remote analysis, and cloud history features fit the stated grooming-analysis purpose, but automatic backend login/registration and token persistence materially broaden the capability beyond simple media analysis.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with pet images/videos or provided URLs being processed by the provider's cloud service, and with the skill silently creating or reusing a backend identity, reading a workspace identity file when present, and storing backend tokens in a local SQLite database for report history.
llm.findings:
[AST7] expected: The dynamic DAO filters are present in generic local persistence code, but I did not find evidence they execute arbitrary code or are exposed directly to untrusted user filter keys in the grooming workflow.
[LP3] unexpected: The least-privilege concern is supported in part: the skill needs file and network access for cloud analysis, but it also includes broad shared API and persistence helpers without a clear permission boundary.
[TP4] unexpected: The artifact does document cloud history and internal identity handling, but automatic account creation/reuse and token handling remain broader than a user would expect from the short grooming-analysis description.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The --export-env-only flag is declared as non-executing behavior, but the script initializes identity and continues normal processing paths instead of honoring a dry-run boundary.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Generic HTTP helpers, backend login/registration, attached auth headers, and stored token/openToken values are present; these are useful for the provider backend but under-scoped for a narrow analysis skill.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The shared SQLite user model and CRUD layer are real and persist identity records in the workspace data area, which is only partially explained by report history support.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger rules are broad but tied to pet grooming media or explicit history-report queries; this is a review note rather than independent evidence of malicious behavior.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The skill discloses server-side analysis, but it does not clearly disclose that local identity files or generated identifiers may be used for backend login/registration and saved tokens.
[E1] unexpected: External transmission to a backend login/registration endpoint is present; it is not theft-like exfiltration, but it is a material under-disclosed side effect.
[P2] expected: The reported zero-width characters occur inside emoji sequences in SKILL.md, not as hidden textual instructions, so I downgrade this finding.
[YR4] expected: The metadata-poisoning signal appears to be driven by the same emoji zero-width joiners and not by concealed routing or trust-manipulation text.
